# Product Requirements: Crypto Hunt

A live, team-based treasure hunt played across a real venue. Teams of four scan hidden QR codes inside the website, solve linked riddles, and race through a shrinking pyramid of rounds to the final treasure.

## Problem

A paper treasure hunt needs volunteers at every spot, is easy to cheat (copy a friend's clue, skip a stop), and the organisers can't see where teams are. Crypto Hunt needs:
- every stop to be checked by the server, so teams can't skip rounds, use another team's QR or guess keys;
- every member of a team to take part, not just one fast player;
- one admin to run and watch the whole hunt live from one panel;
- an audience to follow the race on a projector.

## Target users

| User | Device | What they need |
|---|---|---|
| **Player** (one of 4 in a team) | Own phone, any browser | Join with name + team code, scan QRs inside the site, answer their own question, see the team's clue and map |
| **Admin** (one person) | Laptop (desktop Chrome) | Create teams and codes, generate the game in one click, print QR sheets, start, watch live, set how many teams advance, fix problems |
| **Audience** | Projector (a `/screen` tab) | Live leaderboard, treasure map with team ships, the final treasure-chest opening |

## Goals

1. Run a full hunt from team registration to top 3 with **no manual record keeping**.
2. The admin sees every scan, check-in, answer and alert within **≤ 2 s**.
3. Answers, QR tokens and secret keys are checked **only on the server**. No client ever receives an answer key or another team's target.
4. A team can never complete a round out of order, at another team's QR, or with fewer than all 4 members checked in. **A QR only opens for the round the team is in now** (D-025): finding a later round's QR early gives nothing.
5. Game setup takes **one click** once the locations exist (the generator does the pyramid, links, assignments, questions, keys and print sheet).
6. Supports at least **30 teams (120 players)** in one game.

## Non-goals

- Native apps or installable PWAs. This is **a website only**.
- An AI question generator (D-018). Questions and clues are written by hand.
- Preventing a second phone or a teammate googling. The site warns and alerts instead (D-017).
- Time limits per round or game (D-014).
- More than one game running at the same time.
- Languages other than English.

## Features

See [FEATURES.md](FEATURES.md). Summary:
- Join with name + team code (teams of exactly 4)
- In-site QR scanner + secret key check-in
- Per-member questions that unlock pieces of the location clue
- Ancient treasure map with fog-of-war reveal
- Prank QR codes
- Hints with a 2-minute penalty
- First-X-advance elimination and a top-3 finish
- One-click game generator and printable QR sheet
- Admin live dashboard, controls, overrides, audit log
- Projector screen with live leaderboard, map and a realistic 3D treasure-chest finale
- Bot simulation (dry run)

## Game rules (source of truth)

**Teams**
- The admin creates N teams; each gets a secret team code. Teams are **exactly 4 members** (D-004).
- A player joins with **name + team code**. The 4th member locks the team. A 5th is refused.
- The admin can start only when every team has 4 members (or after removing incomplete teams).

**The pyramid (D-009)**
- The generator builds the rounds. Default QR counts: round 1 = ⌈1.5 × N⌉, then each round = ⌈0.6 × previous⌉ (always at least one fewer), down to **1 final QR**.
  - Example, 10 teams: **15 → 9 → 6 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1** (7 rounds, 40 QRs).
- Every QR in round r links to one QR in round r+1. Several QRs can link to the same one. Each team gets a random round-1 QR; after that its path follows the links.
- Round-1 QRs no team got are **spares** (the admin can re-point a team to one if a QR is damaged).
- **Prank QRs** add about 20% on top of the pyramid QRs (D-016). Example: 8 pranks for 40 QRs.

**A round (one stop, D-010)**
1. **Solve:** each member gets their own question (difficulty rises by round). A correct answer unlocks one of 4 pieces of the clue to the team's QR for this round (D-011).
2. **Seek:** when all 4 pieces are unlocked, the full clue shows and the map fog lifts over the target's region (not the exact spot).
3. **Check in:** at the QR, **each of the 4 members** scans it in the site **and** types its printed secret key (D-008). At the **final QR** each member also types the crew's **seal code** (D-026, see Winning).
4. **Penalty:** if the team used hints, a countdown of 2 minutes per hint runs before the round counts (D-013).
5. **Complete:** the round is done. The next round's questions appear at once.
- Round 1 starts when the admin presses **Start** and each member scans the **universal QR**.
- Questions are a random mix of **multiple choice** (always 4 options, A–D), **one word** and **number** (D-029).
- **Multiple choice:** options are shuffled differently for each player. **One pick:** a wrong pick immediately swaps in a different question (never one the crew has seen); no hint is ever offered.
- **Typed answers:** unlimited attempts, no cooldown. A hidden limit of 10 answers per minute per player stops brute force (also on multiple choice).

**Wrong scans (D-025: round lock)**

A QR opens **only for the round the team is in now**. Nothing a team scans early is saved: when they reach that round they scan it again like everyone else.

| What was scanned | Result |
|---|---|
| A QR from a later round (the team's own future mark **or** anyone else's, including the final QR) | **"Sealed: this mark belongs to a later round."** "You're in Round N. Leave it where it is and follow your own clue." No clue, question, map or key box; never says which round or whether it is on the team's path. A key typed for it anyway is refused on the server (the team isn't in that round). No time penalty. + admin alert on every scan and key try (3 in one round → "possible sweep" alert) |
| A QR from the current round that isn't the team's | "This mark isn't yours. Read your clue again." + admin alert |
| A QR from a round already done | "You've already been here." |
| A spare QR | Same as "isn't yours" |
| A prank QR | "🏆 You reached the final!" → **Get secret key** → "You've been fooled! You're still in Round N." → the team's current clue |
| Anything after elimination | "Your hunt is over." |

**Elimination (D-012)**
- The admin sets **X** (teams that advance) for each round, live. The generator suggests defaults (N down to 3).
- **The moment X teams complete round r, every team that has not completed round r is eliminated, instantly.**
- An eliminated team picks **Game Over** or **Spectator** (live leaderboard) (D-019).

**Winning**
- **Final QR (D-026).** The final QR's printed key is not enough on its own. When a team solves all 4 pieces of the final clue, the server gives that team its own 6-character **seal code** (shown in the clue scroll). At the final QR each member scans, types the printed key **and** types the seal code. Another team's seal code, or any code before the team is in the final round, is refused and alerted.
- The final round has X = 3. The first three teams to complete it are **1st, 2nd, 3rd**. Each gets a unique completion key to show the admin, and the realistic 3D treasure chest opens on their phones and on the projector.
- No time limit (D-014). If the admin presses **End game** early, ranking is: highest round completed, then earliest completion time (penalties included).

**Hints (D-013)**
- Off until the admin turns them on (one click, all teams). A hint is shown to the member who asked. Each hint adds 2 minutes, served at the next check-in.
- **Never on multiple-choice questions** (D-029), even when hints are on.

**Anti-cheat (D-017)**
- Leaving the site while answering shows the player a warning and alerts the admin. No blocking.

**New game (D-020)**
- Typed confirmation. Offers a CSV export, then logs everyone out and deletes players, progress and logs. **Teams are kept with new team codes**, and every team gets a **new random route** at Start. The printed QRs and their keys are kept, so nothing is reprinted. **Optional:** regenerate every QR token and key (the sheet must then be reprinted and rehidden; use it when the same people play again). Locations, map, clues and question bank are kept. Seal codes are always new.

## Workflows

1. **Before the event:** admin logs in → adds locations and pins them on the venue map → sets team count → **Generate game** → prints the QR sheet → hides the QRs.
2. **Registration:** admin hands each team its code → members join → teams lock at 4.
3. **Hunt:** admin presses Start → universal QR shown on the projector → rounds run → admin watches, adjusts X, fixes problems.
4. **Finish:** top 3 complete the final round → chest finale → admin verifies the completion keys on the dashboard.

## Constraints

- A web page cannot stop phone cameras from reading QR codes. All security comes from the server.
- The venue needs one physical spot per QR. **10 teams ≈ 40 pyramid QRs + 8 pranks = 48 spots.**
- Mobile data or WiFi is needed at every spot (user confirmed it is available).
- Vercel cannot hold websockets → Supabase Realtime.

## Success criteria

- Bot simulation: 5/5 runs green with 10 teams × 4 bots and every rule checked at every step.
- Real-device rehearsal at the venue with at least 2 real teams, no blocking issue.
- Admin sees every scan within 2 s; p95 RPC latency < 500 ms.

## Assumptions

- One admin. One game at a time.
- Players are students with modern phones (iOS Safari 16+, Android Chrome).
- Locations and the venue map are supplied by the user near the end of the build (riddles get written then).

## Open questions

- Venue, list of locations and a venue map image (deferred by the user to the end).
- Supabase prod + test projects and Vercel project credentials.
- Rough expected team count (to size the venue spots and seed question bank).
